landmark-ground: Saves written before 2026-10-09 never stored the terrain a template lays under a landmark. Every load lays it back (the layer-1 mountain under the built-in Neighbor Center plaza), so a built-in map gains those cells.
landmark-layout-v3: Save format 3 lays the landmarks at the game's layout sheet: the Neighbor Center moved and grew and the station joined. Every load takes off the objects and terrain a landmark now stands over, then whatever that leaves breaking a post-stroke rule (unsupported blocks, uncontained water), and every object the placement rules refuse where it stands on a landmark's ground or where the load changed the ground under it (a path left uneven at the plaza's raised edge), and reports it as landmark-cleared; the landmark repair the editor asks then sets them back.
history-before-v3: The v2-to-v3 migration drops undo history recorded against the earlier landmark layout, in JSON files and autosave records alike, because undo replays entries without the rules.
ramp-v1-reanchor: Version 1 ramps were four cells long. The v1-to-v2 migration keeps their cliff end, so a ramp rotated 180 or 270 degrees moves its anchor two cells along its run.
share-identity-drift: A share code records the fingerprints of the template and catalog it was made with. A code from a release with another landmark layout or catalog imports with the template-drift and catalog-drift notices.
current-rules: From 2026-10-16 every load holds a map to the current release's full rule set, with no allowance for what the save already held: a terrain cell the rules refuse returns to the template's terrain, what a post-stroke rule then flags gives way, and every object a placement where it stands refuses (a doorstep against a rise, two homes without a cell between them, ground it may not stand on, an overlap) is taken off and reported as landmark-cleared; the repair the editor asks then sets each back at the nearest legal spot or shows it removed.
